title: Piano Movers in Laguna Niguel | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Piano moving company in Laguna Niguel: four movers on one hourly clock, a $200 instrument add-on, and HOA gate and curb rules settled before the day.
heroSubtitle: Four movers, a piano board and straps, and one hourly clock for the whole job.

faq.question: What do you need from my HOA or guard gate before the move?
faq.answer: Send the crew through your association first. At communities like Ocean Ranch, guards admit guests, vendors and service personnel only on a resident’s authorization, so the owner’s name and the address have to be on the list before the truck reaches the entrance. If the association or the building asks for a certificate of insurance, that is $50 and we issue it in advance.

faq.question: Where does the truck stand while the instrument comes out?
faq.answer: On the driveway whenever the driveway takes it. City code keeps commercial vehicles over 80 inches wide or 25 feet long off public streets in a residence district, bans them citywide between 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., and posted sweeping signs close some frontages from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. We agree the truck position with you before the day so the carry starts immediately.

faq.question: How is the instrument billed if the whole house moves the same day?
faq.answer: It runs on the same hourly clock as everything else. A crew of four is $199 an hour in cash or $209 by card Monday through Thursday, $215 or $225 Friday through Sunday, with a three-hour minimum, and the instrument adds a flat $200 to that bill. There is no second invoice and no separate rate for the piano.

faq.question: Can you move a piano in Laguna Niguel today?
faq.answer: Often yes, when a crew of four is open. Booking hours run Monday through Sunday, 8AM to 6PM, and drive time from our Los Angeles base counts toward the job, so an early call gives the best chance of a same-day slot. Call 909-443-0004 and we will check the board with you.

faq.question: Do you tune, appraise or dispose of pianos?
faq.answer: No. We move instruments and nothing else around them: tuning, valuation and disposal belong to a technician or a dealer, and we do not quote them. What we cover is the handling — the board, the straps, the pads, the stairs and the tie-down in the truck.
